newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia to privatise timber firm Zambezi Sawmills.
newsitem.headline: Zambia to privatise timber firm Zambezi Sawmills.

text.p: The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Wednesday it was offering for sale 100 percent of state-run forestry company Zambezi Sawmills in an ongoing privatisation programme.
Zambezi Sawmills, with recent annual sales of between $600,000 and $900,000, has its headquarters and timber mills in the southern town of Livingstone, bordering Zimbabwe.
It also has two other sawmills in Sesheke and Mulobezi in western and southern Zambia respectively.
Sales consist mainly of railway/mining sleepers, cross beams for telephone poles, parquet, sawn timber and some finished furniture.
"Historically, major companies such as Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines and Zambia Railways have accounted for most of the sales," a ZPA spokesman said.
"However, there is a growing demand for specialised wood products worldwide and from neighbouring countries, particularly South Africa."
The company, with a workforce of 190, has a five-year concession to extract wood for government land, which expires in two years.
